Dimension reduction serves to constrain the estimated βj coefficients, since now they must take the form (6.18). This constraint on the form of the coefficients has the potential to bias the coefficient estimates. However, in situations where p is large relative to n, selecting a value of M ≪p can significantly reduce the variance of the fitted coefficients. If M = p, and all the Zm are linearly independent, then (6.18) poses no constraints.
